title: Row order: groups, joins and `unique` keep no order unless asked
verdict: order only with `maintain_order`; a join's default order may change between runs
description: `group_by` keeps the order of the groups consistent with the input only with `maintain_order=True` (which the streaming engine runs: its group_by adds a row index, takes its first value per group and sorts the groups by it); rows within a group always keep their order. A join's `maintain_order` defaults to `"none"`: the ordering might differ across Polars versions or between runs, and the docs say not to rely on an observed order.

Float sums depend on the summation tree: pairwise, Kahan when grouped, plain across chunks (polars-sum-float), so chunking and the thread count can change their last bits. The docs do not say so; `sum` only documents that small integers are cast to Int64.

Round 2 (source), streaming engine: a grouped `sum` is a `NumSumReducer` whose `combine` adds the partial sums; within a morsel a float column is summed pairwise (`ChunkAgg::sum`), per group row by row. The reducer is marked `ORDER_INDEPENDENT`, which the trait documents as "changing the result by at most floating-point rounding" when the values of a group are split into several states. The group-by sink builds pre-aggregates per pipeline and combines them partition by partition in the order they were produced, so the morsel distribution over threads decides the order of the float additions. Probes at POLARS_MAX_THREADS 1 and N go to the next round.
No upstream test pins the float sums' variation with the thread count; it may change between versions.
reference: The reference compares results as bags, so row order outside a sort is free; `sum_order` is open and allowed within the plan's bound (polars-sum-float).

evidence.note: NumSumReducer: combine adds, floats summed pairwise per morsel
pre-aggregates combined into the partition's table
partitions built from the pre-aggregates in order

notes: s-group-order: the first group keys of `group_by('g').len()` over 100 000 rows were [274, 396, 39, …] in memory and [0, 919, 838, …] streaming, and neither is the input order; both engines give an arbitrary order. s-group-fsum-runs: five runs of a grouped sum over 300 000 rows gave several results on both engines. s-fsum-runs and s-var-runs: the ungrouped streaming sum and variance vary between runs (polars-sum-float-streaming, polars-var-std-streaming); in memory they did not.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each observation (`STREAMING_OBSERVATIONS`, python/tools/sverify_dev/probe_polars.py) with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')` and records both results. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

provenance.notes: Rerun on small inputs (3,000 or 5,000 rows) in a subprocess with POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=64 and POLARS_SORT_PARTITION_THRESHOLD_BYTES=1024, which Polars reads at start-up: the same behaviour as the large inputs at the defaults (the unstable streaming sort, sums and var varying by run), so the probes stay cheap. The variables only move the thresholds; the large-input results at the defaults stand.

then the groups are sorted by it: maintain_order runs on the streaming engine
only the sorted-keys fast path declines unsorted keys with maintain_order

provenance.notes: Corrected the description: it said `maintain_order=True` blocks the streaming engine. At py-2.1.0 the streaming group_by handles it (lower_group_by.rs#L930-L941, #L1190-L1205); the docs' "blocks the possibility to run partitioned" is about the distributed engine.
